perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Nebius disclosed a May 20, 2026 agreement with Bloom Energy for 328 MW of behind-the-meter fuel-cell capacity planned operational in 2026. The architecture is explicitly intended to shorten time-to-power and reduce dependence on new transmission build, addressing a material AI-infrastructure bottleneck with a named supplier and quantified planned capacity.

risks: Planned power capacity is not the same as commissioned capacity; delivery, fuel availability, site integration and data-center commissioning remain execution dependencies.
unknowns: The announcement does not establish realized uptime, delivered MW, unit power economics, or whether the full 328 MW was operational by this evidence date.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: capitalExecution
factors.basis: Nebius also disclosed on March 3, 2026 that Independence, Missouri approved the Chapter 100 industrial-development incentive plan for its planned AI-factory campus, enabling construction to proceed at a site with potential capacity up to 1.2 GW. Together with the separately contracted 328 MW Bloom power deployment, this provides source-addressed evidence of site/permitting and power-procurement execution rather than demand announcements alone.

risks: Municipal approval and contracted power do not prove construction completion, GPU installation, customer utilization, margins or returns on invested capital.
unknowns: Actual construction progress and commissioned capacity at Independence are not established by these two announcements.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. newsroom / Bloom Energy power partnership announcement
facts: Nebius and Bloom Energy announced an agreement to deploy Bloom fuel-cell technology for Nebius AI infrastructure.
The announcement states 328 MW of installed capacity was planned to be operational in 2026.
Nebius described the behind-the-meter system as reducing dependence on new transmission build and shortening time-to-power.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. newsroom / Independence Missouri AI-factory approval announcement
facts: Independence City Council approved the Chapter 100 industrial-development incentive plan for Nebius's planned AI-factory campus.
Nebius said the approval enables it to proceed with construction.
The planned campus has potential capacity of up to 1.2 GW.

result: Materially different site-and-power execution evidence packaged for Alpha. It source-addresses supply-chain resilience and execution capacity while explicitly separating approvals/plans from commissioned operating capacity.
